title: Adam Robinson's free course: take a SaaS from $0 to $10M ARR bootstrapped with a tiny team
summary: Adam Robinson lays out the "sell before you build" framework: pre-sell with a sizzling one-liner and quick pitch, build a manual MVP, find product-market fit through hundreds of calls, and stay tiny. The second half covers getting unstuck from $1M to $10M, hiring almost nobody, inbound-led outbound, and refusing VC money.

principles.text: Sell before you build: pre-sell the idea to real buyers first.
principles.quote: Elite founders do not start developing anything before they have buyers of what they're about to build.

principles.text: Do things that don't scale until you have PMF; skip growth hacking, ads, SEO and partnerships.
principles.quote: Nothing will work if you don't have product market fit. Everything will work if you do have product market fit.

principles.text: Money is the honest signal; getting people to pay beats nice words about your idea.
principles.quote: The single best way to figure out if someone actually likes your idea is get them to hand you money.

principles.text: Do not hire anyone before $1M ARR; aim for $10M ARR with no more than 10 employees.
principles.quote: Do not hire anybody before 1 million ARR. Co-founders only.

principles.text: When stuck above $1M, go all in on your lowest-churn segment and ignore everyone else.
principles.quote: If you can identify a segment with significantly lower churn, go all in on them. That's your new ICP.

principles.text: Pipeline comes from creating original demand, then selling only to people who visited your site.
principles.quote: These STRs don't create demand. They were only capturing demand created elsewhere.
